spec.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
spec.conclusion: V(K) is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W of V(K), if W is invariant under the induced operators x,y,h then W={0} or W=V(K). Equivalently V(K) is a nonzero irreducible L(K)-module.

V(K)=M⊗_Z K. Here tensor products have their usual balanced-module meaning: they are generated by pure tensors subject to additivity in each argument and (am)⊗c=m⊗(ac) for the base scalar a. Induced lattice endomorphisms act on the M factor; the same symbols x,y,h denote these induced K-linear operators once preservation of M is established.

L(K) is the scalar extension to K of the free rank-three Chevalley Z-Lie algebra on formal basis ξ,η,ζ, with brackets [ζ,ξ]=2ξ, [ζ,η]=-2η, [ξ,η]=ζ, extended bilinearly and antisymmetrically with zero self-brackets. This is (Zx+Zy+Zh)⊗_Z K in the original notation, with ξ,η,ζ labeled there by x,y,h. These are abstract Chevalley generators, not their possibly nonfaithful operator images on V. The generators ξ⊗1,η⊗1,ζ⊗1 act on V(K) by the operators x,y,h induced from M. This is the Chevalley construction also in characteristic 2.

propositions.statement: Let A and B be commutative semirings, S a multiplicative submonoid of A, and B an A-algebra which is a localization of A at S. Let T be an additive commutative monoid and A-module. Then the A-linear map f:T→B⊗_A T, f(t)=1⊗t, is a localized-module map at S: (i) multiplication by each s∈S on B⊗_A T is a unit in its semiring of A-linear endomorphisms; (ii) for every z∈B⊗_A T there exist t∈T and s∈S with sz=f(t); (iii) f(t₁)=f(t₂) implies that st₁=st₂ for some s∈S. A localization B at S means the images of S are units, every element has a numerator in A and denominator in S, and equality of images of two elements of A is killed by some element of S.

The integer map Z→K extends to a ring map R→K by a/d↦(a in K)/(d in K). There are natural K-linear isomorphisms M⊗_Z K≃M_R⊗_R K≃(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{F_p}K, where F_p=Z/pZ and its map to K is induced by the integer map. All binom(λ,j) and all r! for 0≤r≤λ are nonzero in K; induced divided powers satisfy X_r=(r!)^{-1}x^r and Y_r=(r!)^{-1}y^r in that range, and ε_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1} X_{λ-i}(Y_λX_λ)Y_{λ-j}. locals.declaration: Use t as the induction index for the formulas on y^t v, beginning at t=0.
Fix arbitrary complex coefficients c indexed by I to test a linear relation.

argument.text: H001 gives n>0 and the finite index set I. From H002 and H003, induction on t gives hy^t v=(λ-2t)y^t v and, for t≥1, xy^t v=t(λ-t+1)y^{t-1}v. Indeed h y=y h-2y gives the h step. For x, the base is xyv=yxv+hv=λv; if xy^t v=t(λ-t+1)y^{t-1}v, then xy^{t+1}v=yxy^t v+hy^t v=[t(λ-t+1)+λ-2t]y^t v=(t+1)(λ-t)y^t v. The t=0 h identity is hv=λv. Iterating the x identity, for 0≤i≤λ, gives x^i y^i v=i! λ(λ-1)⋯(λ-i+1)v≠0: every factor is a positive integer when i>0, and the empty product is 1 when i=0. Thus e_i≠0 for every i∈I.

produces.statement: For every s≥0, hy^s v=(λ-2s)y^s v, and for s≥1, xy^s v=s(λ-s+1)y^{s-1}v. Every e_i for i∈I is nonzero.

argument.text: Take arbitrary c:I→C and temporarily assume L1: ∑_{i∈I} c_i e_i=0. For each j∈I, apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h-(λ-2k)Id_V). F001 makes every summand except the j-th vanish, leaving c_j ∏_{k≠j}2(k-j)e_j=0. Its vector and scalar factors are nonzero over C, so c_j=0. Discharge L1; the family e is linearly independent. H002 gives dim_C V=n=card(I), so M003 makes its span all of V. Independence and spanning are precisely the basis conditions. The h formula at t=λ+1 has eigenvalue -λ-2. Expanding y^{λ+1}v in this basis and comparing coefficients in h gives [-λ-2-(λ-2i)] times its i-th coefficient equal to zero. These multipliers are nonzero for all i∈I, hence y^{λ+1}v=0. Further powers vanish by applying y.

produces.statement: e is a complex basis of V, and y^{λ+1}v and every higher y-power on v vanish.

argument.text: Divide the identities in F001 by i! and use F002 to obtain xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_{i-1} for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. For any r≥0, iterate these formulas r times and divide by r!: for r≤i the x coefficient is (λ-i+1)⋯(λ-i+r)/r!=binom(λ-i+r,r), and for i+r≤λ the y coefficient is (i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!=binom(i+r,r). Outside those ranges the string has already hit zero, so the result is zero. These binomial coefficients are integers (for example their usual counting interpretation as r-element subsets of a finite set proves integrality). At r=0 both products equal 1. This proves the full characteristic-zero coordinate statement.

argument.text: By H004 choose an integer basis m indexed by A which is also a complex basis. It is finite because V has the finite basis N001. M002 over C gives card(A)=dim_C V=card(I)=n. Reindexing by a bijection therefore permits an I-indexed basis. M001, with scalar extension Z→R, gives an R-basis (1⊗m_a) of R⊗_Z M. The multiplication map r⊗m↦rm sends this basis to the same vectors m_a in V. Their complex independence implies R-independence, and their R-span is M_R by definition. Thus this map is injective and onto M_R, and the images form an R-basis with n elements, reindexed by I.

argument.text: Every X_r and Y_r preserves M by H004 and D006. By complex linearity, it preserves the R-span M_R. Also M_R contains the basis vectors m_a, so its complex span is V, as recorded in F001. These statements do not restrict M to the minimal lattice.

argument.text: Define Qop=Y_λ X_λ. Test N001 on every e_k: X_λ kills k<λ and sends e_λ to e_0, while Y_λ e_0=e_λ; hence Qop=E_{λλ}. Likewise X_{λ-i}Qop=E_{iλ}, since X_{λ-i}e_λ=e_i. Finally Qop Y_{λ-j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}: an input e_k with k<j lands below e_λ and is killed by Qop; one with k>j passes the end of the y-string and vanishes; at k=j the coefficient is binom(λ,λ-j)=binom(λ,j). These identities hold for all i,j∈I, including λ=0.

produces.statement: Qop=E_{λλ}, X_{λ-i}Qop=E_{iλ}, and Qop Y_{λ-j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj} for every i,j∈I.

argument.text: For every j∈I, H001 and M007 show p divides none of λ!, j!, (λ-j)!. These integers therefore have inverses in R by its denominator definition. The identity binom(λ,j)=λ!/(j!(λ-j)!) makes this binomial a unit in R. Composing F003 gives X_{λ-i}Qop Y_{λ-j}=binom(λ,j)E_ij, whence E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ-i}(Y_λX_λ)Y_{λ-j}. F002 and closure of the R-module M_R under R-scalars prove preservation by every E_ij. F001 supplies the basis and scalar-extension assertions. No reduced h-eigenvalue argument has been used.

argument.text: For i∈I, E_ii maps M_R onto J_i e_i: its image is contained there by N002 and the coordinate formula, and it fixes every vector c e_i in that module. For i,j∈I, applying E_ij to c e_j proves J_j⊆J_i; interchanging indices proves equality. Thus J_i=J_0=J. Every vector in M_R is the sum of its E_ii projections, and the independence of e in N001 makes this sum direct. Therefore M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i. Each summand is generated by the projections of the finite basis in N002. Since e_i≠0, multiplication by e_i identifies J with this summand, so J is finitely generated. J cannot be zero: otherwise M_R=0 would contradict its complex span being V and the nonzero basis N001 with n>0 from H001.

produces.statement: J_i=J for all i∈I; J is a nonzero finitely generated R-submodule of C, and M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i.

argument.text: Define T=Q⊗_R J and μ:T→C by μ(q⊗c)=qc; balancing makes this a Q-linear map. Q is a localization of R at its nonzero elements: nonzero elements become units, every rational is a numerator/denominator with both in R (indeed integers suffice), and equality in Q is equality in the subring R, so the equality-killing condition holds with 1. M004 then says every z∈T satisfies sz=1⊗c for some c∈J and nonzero s∈R. Consequently μ(z)=c/s. If μ(z)=0, then c=0 in C, hence in J, so sz=0 and z=0 since s is invertible over Q. Thus μ is injective and its image is exactly the rational span of J. A finite R-generating list of J from F001 gives a finite Q-spanning list of T, because z=s^{-1}(1⊗c) and c is an R-combination of that list. Hence T is finite-dimensional.

produces.statement: T is finite-dimensional over Q and μ:T→C is injective with image span_Q J.

argument.text: Define r=finrank_Q T. Tensoring the direct decomposition F001 yields a Q-linear equivalence Q⊗_R M_R≃∏_{i∈I}T. Explicitly, on a pure tensor q₀⊗m, take its i-th coordinate to be q₀⊗c_i, where m=∑ c_i e_i with c_i∈J. The inverse takes a tuple whose entries are finite sums of q⊗c to the sum of the tensors q⊗(c e_i). Coordinate extraction is R-linear; these prescriptions are balanced and additive, and their composites fix pure tensors and tuples of pure tensors, hence all finite sums, so they are inverse. M001 applied to the I-indexed R-basis of M_R supplied by N002 gives an I-indexed Q-basis of Q⊗_R M_R; M002 gives its dimension n. M008 gives freeness of T over Q, while F002 gives finite generation. Thus M006 gives dimension of ∏_I T equal to ∑_I r=nr, and M005 applied to the displayed equivalence gives n=nr. Since n=λ+1>0 by H001, r=1.

produces.statement: finrank_Q T=1, with T finite-dimensional and μ injective.

argument.text: By F001 choose 0≠a∈J and a finite nonzero generating list g_1,...,g_k of J, with k≥1. The vector 1⊗a in T is nonzero because its μ-image is a. Thus this singleton is Q-linearly independent (a scalar multiple equal to zero has scalar zero). F003 and M003 show that it spans T. For each 1≤j≤k, write 1⊗g_j as q_j(1⊗a) and apply μ to get g_j=q_j a. Since g_j≠0, q_j≠0. In particular all generators lie in the one-dimensional rational line Q a; this conclusion uses the rank computation, not merely the inclusion J⊂C.

produces.statement: There exists a family qcoefs of nonzero rational numbers indexed by {1,...,k} such that g_j=qcoefs_j a for every 1≤j≤k.

argument.text: Choose the family q from F004. Each nonzero rational q_j can be written p^{ν_j}u_j with ν_j∈Z and u_j a unit in R. To see existence without assuming a rank-one ideal theorem, write the rational as a ratio of two nonzero integers. For a positive integer d, divide off p repeatedly while it divides d. This terminates: p≥2 by H001, so each division of a positive divisible integer strictly decreases it; equivalently induction on d supplies a largest nonnegative exponent with remaining positive factor not divisible by p. Apply this to the absolute values of numerator and denominator; keep their signs in the remaining factors. Subtract the two exponents to get ν_j. The remaining ratio and its inverse both have denominators not divisible by p, hence belong to R, giving the unit u_j. Applying this finite construction to all indices gives the families in F005.

produces.statement: There exist integer exponents exps_j and units units_j∈R, for 1≤j≤k, with q_j=p^{exps_j}units_j.

argument.text: Choose νs and u from F005; let ν be their finite minimum and set b=p^ν a≠0. For every j, g_j=q_j a=p^{νs_j-ν}u_j b∈Rb, since νs_j-ν≥0. Conversely an index attaining the minimum gives g_j=u_j b, so b=u_j^{-1}g_j∈J. Thus J=Rb. This proves the required existential statement. F001 gives spanning of M_R by (b e_i), and N001 gives their R-independence: a relation divided by the nonzero complex scalar b is a relation on e. Hence they form an R-basis. The same proof applies to every nonzero scalar that generates J over R, since it uses only that scalar's nonzeroness and its generating property. F001, F002 and F003 provide the direct decomposition, injectivity of the tensor multiplication map, and dimension one.

applications.bindings: A=R, S=R\{0}, B=Q, source T=J, and f(c)=1⊗c.
hypothesis_checks: R⊂Q is a commutative ring by H001 and D007; its nonzero elements form a multiplicative submonoid since it is a domain, and Q is its commutative algebra.
The numerator, denominator and equality conditions are verified explicitly earlier in S002 using R⊂Q and integer fractions.
J is an R-submodule of C by D011; it is an additive commutative group and R-module.

applications.bindings: A=R, B=Q, source T=M_R, C=I, and d any I-indexed R-basis supplied by N002.
hypothesis_checks: R and Q are commutative rings with the inclusion algebra structure.
M_R is an R-submodule of V by D008.
N002 supplies the I-indexed basis, and the formula applies for every i∈I.

applications.bindings: A=Q, source T=Q⊗_R M_R, C=I and d the scalar-extension basis delivered by M001.
hypothesis_checks: Q is a field, hence satisfies the strong rank condition.
The tensor product is a Q-vector space.
M001 earlier in S003 supplies the basis; I is finite with card(I)=n by H001 and D002.

applications.bindings: A=Q, source T=Q⊗_R M_R, U=∏_{i∈I}T, f=the coordinate tensor equivalence displayed in S003.
hypothesis_checks: Both sides are Q-vector spaces.
The maps are explicitly balanced linear maps, with inverse composites checked on generators earlier in S003.

applications.bindings: A=Q, C=I, and every component T_c equal to the local space T=Q⊗_R J.
hypothesis_checks: Q is a field and satisfies the strong rank condition.
I is finite with n indices.
T is a Q-vector space; M008 earlier in S003 gives freeness and F002 gives finite generation by a finite spanning list.
Q is a division ring and T=Q⊗_R J is a Q-vector space with additive commutative group.

applications.bindings: A=Q, source T=local T, C=a singleton, d its sole vector 1⊗a.
hypothesis_checks: T is a Q-vector space.
F002 gives finite dimension, and a singleton is finite.
The μ-image of 1⊗a is nonzero a, so the singleton is independent by field scalar cancellation.
Its cardinality is 1, equal to dim_Q T by F003.

locals.declaration: Choose b≠0 in J with J=Rb, using N003.
Define ρ(a/d)=(a in K)/(d in K) for p not dividing d; well-definedness is established in S001.
Define F_p=Z/pZ with its natural map to K.
Define β_i to be the image of (b e_i)⊗1 under the inverse of the first isomorphism constructed in S002.
After establishing in S003 that β is a basis, define ε_ij by ε_ij β_k=δ_jk β_i.

argument.text: Choose b as in N003. Since K has characteristic p by H001, the kernel of Z→K is pZ: Euclidean division by p reduces any integer to a remainder 0≤s<p, and the definition of characteristic says no positive such remainder maps to zero. Consequently any integer d not divisible by p has nonzero image in K. Define ρ(a/d)=a_K/d_K on R. Equality of fractions is cross-multiplication in Z, hence in K; their denominators remain nonzero, proving well-definedness, additivity and multiplicativity. Thus ρ extends the integer map. Its kernel is pR, since a/d maps to zero exactly when p divides a. Reduction sends a/d modulo p to a times the inverse of d in F_p=Z/pZ, giving R/pR≃F_p with the natural inclusion F_p→K. The latter is injective by the same characteristic argument. Also X_1=x and Y_1=y preserve M by H004; H002 gives h=xy-yx, so h preserves M too. All induced lattice actions in D012 are therefore defined.

produces.statement: ρ:R→K is a well-defined ring map extending Z→K with kernel pR, and R/pR≃F_p=Z/pZ compatibly with the natural injection F_p→K. The operators x,y,h preserve M.

argument.text: Use N002 to identify M_R with R⊗_Z M. The first isomorphism sends m⊗c in M⊗_Z K to m⊗c in M_R⊗_R K, equivalently (1⊗m)⊗c. Its inverse sends (r⊗m)⊗c to m⊗ρ(r)c. Integer and R-balancing verify both maps, and their composites fix every pure tensor, hence all finite sums. For the second isomorphism send u⊗c to (u+pM_R)⊗c. The inverse sends (u+pM_R)⊗c to u⊗c; changing u by pz changes the result by z⊗pc=0. Balancing over F_p follows from F000 and the R-action through R/pR; the same pure tensor check shows inverse composites. These maps are K-linear and intertwine every induced R-linear lattice operator, as is checked on pure tensors.

produces.statement: There are K-linear isomorphisms V(K)=M⊗_Z K≃M_R⊗_R K≃(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{F_p}K with exactly the maps displayed in S002; they intertwine all induced lattice operators.

argument.text: N003 says (b e_i) is an R-basis of M_R. Applying M001 with R→K makes the vectors 1⊗(b e_i) a K-basis of K⊗_R M_R. The flip of pure tensors, c⊗u↔u⊗c, is balanced and has itself as inverse, so it identifies this basis with (b e_i)⊗1 in M_R⊗_R K. Transporting through F001 defines β_i and proves β is a K-basis of V(K). Reduction of the R-basis modulo p is also a basis over F_p: its coordinates identify M_R with R^I and pM_R with (pR)^I, hence the quotient with (R/pR)^I. The second isomorphism in F001 therefore gives the same basis by reduction and extension. N001 applied to b e_i (b is a complex scalar) gives exactly xβ_0=0, xβ_i=(λ-i+1)β_{i-1}, yβ_i=(i+1)β_{i+1} for i<λ, yβ_λ=0, hβ_i=(λ-2i)β_i, with the boundary restrictions on x as in N001 and all coefficients mapped to K. Define ε_ij to be the matrix units for this basis. By N002, E_ij preserve M_R and hence induce these ε_ij, and their product identities persist by F001.

produces.statement: β is a K-basis of V(K) obtained from b e_i by the scalar-extension maps. Its operator formulas are xβ_0=0, xβ_i=(λ-i+1)β_{i-1} for i≥1, yβ_i=(i+1)β_{i+1} for i<λ, yβ_λ=0, hβ_i=(λ-2i)β_i, for i∈I. Induced E_ij are ε_ij, and ε_ij=ρ(binom(λ,j))^{-1} X_{λ-i}(Y_λX_λ)Y_{λ-j}, where X,Y here denote induced divided-power operators.

argument.text: For each 0≤r≤λ<p, M007 gives p not dividing r!, so its image in K is nonzero by F000. On the original lattice r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r, and both sides preserve M. Thus after scalar extension X_r=(r!)^{-1}x^r and Y_r=(r!)^{-1}y^r in this range. N002 states binom(λ,j) is a unit in R; its image in K is a unit since ρ sends its inverse to an inverse. F002 therefore gives ε_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ-i}(Y_λX_λ)Y_{λ-j}. A subspace invariant under x,y is invariant under their nonnegative powers, scalar multiples and compositions, so this formula proves its invariance under every ε_ij. All indices used here lie between 0 and λ. The argument works for any witness b allowed by N003, establishing the stated universal assertions.

applications.bindings: A=R, B=K with algebra map ρ, T=M_R, C=I, d_i=b e_i.
hypothesis_checks: R and K are commutative rings and F000 proves the ring map ρ.
M_R is an R-module by D008.
N003 and the witness b from S001 give the R-basis d_i=b e_i.
H001 gives prime p and 0≤r≤λ<p, so the source equivalence excludes p dividing r!.

locals.type: K-basis of V(K) indexed by I
locals.declaration: Choose the K-basis β with matrix-unit identities supplied by N004.
Define ε_ij to be the matrix units of the chosen basis β as in N004.
Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W of V(K).
In the nonzero branch choose w≠0 in W using F001 under L2.
Let c be the unique coordinate family of w in the basis β.
Choose j with c_j≠0; equivalently choose the index of a nonzero coordinate of w whose existence is in F001.

argument.text: Choose β and define ε as in N004; H001 gives n=λ+1>0, so I is nonempty. The basis vector β_0 is nonzero, proving V(K)≠0. Fix an arbitrary subspace W and assume L1: W is invariant under x,y,h. N004 then makes W invariant under every ε_ij. If W={0}, the desired alternative is already true. In the other branch assume L2: W≠{0}. By this assumption W has a nonzero vector; since β is a basis, such a vector has a nonzero coordinate. Record F001 to choose both a vector and an index in the next paragraph.

produces.statement: There exist a nonzero vector z∈W and an index t∈I such that the t-th coordinate of z in β is nonzero. Also W is invariant under every ε_{ii,jj} for ii,jj∈I.

argument.text: Choose the vector w and index j jointly from F001 and let w=∑_{i∈I}c_i β_i be its basis expansion, so c_j≠0. For every i∈I, the matrix-unit formula gives ε_ij w=c_j β_i∈W. Since K is a field, multiplication by c_j^{-1} gives β_i∈W. Every vector of V(K) is a K-linear combination of these basis vectors, so W=V(K). Thus in the nonzero branch the required alternative holds; discharge L2 and combine with the zero branch to get W={0} or W=V(K) under L1.

Discharge L1 and universally quantify the arbitrary W. Together with nonzeroness proved in S001 this proves the asserted subspace statement. For the Lie-algebra formulation, H004 and H002 give lattice preservation of x,y and h=xy-yx, so L(K) acts as defined; invariance under its generator span is equivalent, by linearity, to invariance under x,y,h. Hence the same statement is irreducibility as an L(K)-module. No algebraic closure of K was used. When λ=0, n=1 and all factorials and binomials in the route are 1; the proof remains valid. When p=2, H001 permits λ=0 or 1 and all factorials used have r<2. No distinctness of reduced h-eigenvalues was invoked.
